title: Westward Ho

evidence.note: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, Jan-Dec 1963 (Vol 17, Parts 12-13), Renewal Registrations: 'WESTWARD HO, a photoplay in seven reels by Republic Pictures Corp. © 7Aug35; L5705. Republic Corp. (PWH); R3189350.' This is the 1935 Republic film: the original registration is dated 7 Aug 1935 and the renewal was filed in the film's 28th-year window, so the copyright was renewed.

editorial:
Westward Ho (1935) is a seven-reel Western that Republic Pictures Corp. registered for copyright on 7 August 1935 (L5705). It stars John Wayne and was made at Republic, which owned the film as a work made for hire. A creator would want it for its Wayne footage and its 1930s Western imagery.

The rights trap is that the copyright was renewed. The 1963 Catalog of Copyright Entries lists a renewal in Republic Corp.'s name, R3189350. That renewal falls in the film's 28th-year window, so the print is not in the public domain on a lapsed-renewal theory. Copies that circulate online as 'public domain' do not change that. Treat any reuse as needing a license from the current rights holder, and do not rely on a free-to-use claim from a hosting site.
faq: No. The Catalog of Copyright Entries for 1963 lists a renewal for the film, R3189350, filed in Republic Corp.'s name against the original 7 August 1935 registration. Because it was renewed, it is not free on a missing-renewal basis.
Can I use clips from a free online copy?

Not safely. A copy being freely available online does not affect the renewed copyright. Clearing clips means finding the current owner of Republic's rights, since the renewal was in Republic Corp.'s name.
